body.x: Gbrain Co., Ltd. (Co-CEOs Byoung Kim and Sunggu Yang) announced that it will participate in CES 2026, to be held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9, as part of the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion.

Gbrain is a Korean startup founded in 2019 to develop treatments for intractable brain disorders. The company has built capabilities step by step across research and development, manufacturing, quality control, and clinical processes, centered on cortical electrodes implanted directly into patients and brain neural stimulation technologies. It completed a production system for related products and obtained GMP certification for its manufacturing facility last year.

In addition, Gbrain secured a national R&D project to develop fully implantable closed-loop brain neural stimulation technology and has since accelerated its research and development efforts. Through this process, the company has advanced its core technologies and verified clinical applicability. By demonstrating both technological competitiveness and business potential, Gbrain has attracted approximately 8 billion won in investment to date.

‘Phin Stim,’ Gbrain’s R&D outcome and its CES 2026 exhibit, is a fully implantable brain neural stimulator that integrates ultra-thin, highly flexible cortical electrodes with circuitry in a single structure. The proprietary electrodes are designed to closely adhere to the cortical surface, enabling stable acquisition of high-resolution brain signals. The collected signals are immediately processed within the device and used to support clinicians’ treatment decisions.

The core of Phin Stim lies in the AI-based signal-processing technology embedded in its circuitry. This technology analyzes brain waves in real time to assess the patient’s current neural state and automatically adjusts stimulation parameters accordingly. While conventional deep brain stimulation relies on repeatedly delivering pre-set stimulation, Gbrain has implemented a closed-loop treatment concept in which stimulation dynamically and automatically adapts to changes in patient condition.

The system is also designed to support brain-signal–based stimulation control and functional expansion via brain–computer interface (BCI) technology. As a result, it offers scalability toward a wide range of future neurological indications and effectively complements the limitations of traditional neural stimulation therapies, according to the company.

A Gbrain official said, “At CES, we plan to introduce our implantable brain medical device technology and the business vision built around it to the global market, while seeking potential partners for overseas expansion.” The official added, “In particular, we aim to discuss and explore collaboration opportunities with global medical device companies, hospitals, and research institutions, focusing on fully implantable brain neural stimulation technology and BCI-based approaches.”

The official continued, “At the same time, using CES 2026 as a turning point, our goal is to review the clinical scalability and range of technological applications demanded by the global market and to establish the foundation for global clinical trials and comprehensive commercialization.”

Incheon Metropolitan City and the Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority announced that they will establish the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion in the LVCC North Hall at CES 2026, showcasing Incheon’s urban vision and innovative technologies as the city evolves from smart city development into the AI era. By linking various exhibition programs—including the 10 companies participating in the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion, Eureka Park, global pavilions, and the CES Innovation Award Showcase—the organizations will support the participation of 51 Incheon-based innovative companies at CES. Notably, 14 companies received CES Innovation Awards across 17 categories, marking a record-high achievement and demonstrating the technological competitiveness and global growth potential of Incheon’s innovation companies.
